{"self_assessment": "**Impact**
I proposed the fish early, with a single run from the nose splitting over the top and bottom of the body and meeting at a forked tail. The table adopted it straight away, so we spent the 10 minutes building rather than debating. Near the end about 151 of 205 standing dominoes were connected to the start. The body and both fins should fall, and the fish should be recognizable. I can't say how it came out, since I haven't seen the result of the push. The middle loops stayed unconnected and wasted some dominoes. I started building one of them before Hana told me to stop, and that was my mistake.

**Execution**
I laid the top body line and checked the tail join. When Omar's bottom line was still short, I built the back half from the tail and closed the gap where we met. I also fixed the off-line bit before the tail. I took out a jammed domino at the start of the upper fin and closed the gap into it. One nudge placed nothing, so I inspected the spot to find the cause. Hana, not me, caught the biggest problem, the gap between the start domino and the nose. I should have checked that early on, since it would have stopped almost everything falling. We also finished with some loop dominoes unused and unconnected.

**Collaboration**
I kept my messages specific about where I was working and asked others to keep clear of that spot. I took Hana's direction on the loop and on the tail cleanup. Omar and I split the bottom line and met in the middle. Hana and Jack both worked on the fins and had some overlap and confusion over who had which one, which cost us time. I should have helped sort that out sooner.

**Leadership**
I set the plan and assigned the strokes, but Hana ended up running the checks and coordination. I did not catch the start gap and I helped with fixes rather than leading them. I would rate myself solid but not top, and Hana's catches were the most important contribution."}
